# Canva 429 explained


By OpenTools Team


·


November 6, 2026


Credits aren’t capacity.


##


Request


Canva’s[November 5 changelog](https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/rest-apis/changelog/) adds` model_capacity_reached` (429) for **Create image generation job** . October’s credit changes use 402:` credit_quota_exceeded` identifies the user allowance,` app_credit_quota_exceeded` the app’s. Waiting for model capacity does not resolve exhausted credits.


Canva’s[error guide](https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/rest-apis/error-responses/) prescribes exponential backoff for` too_many_requests` . Keep status and code distinct in logs; routing by 429 alone conflates capacity with throttling.


##


Job


The[preview endpoint](https://www.canva.dev/docs/apps/rest-apis/reference/generations/create-image-generation-job/) can return HTTP 200 before completion. Inspect job status.


The required` idempotency_key` replays the original job for 24 hours despite parameter changes. Changing models under that key does not start replacement work. Check identity. Documentation analysis; no API test.


For creator‑facing availability, see our[Craft report](https://opentools.ai/news/canva-craft-dream-lab-image-generation-api-mcp-coming-soon) .
